jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: No national AI law, strategy or AI guidance from the Myanmar government has been identified on official sites. The telecommunications regulator under the communications ministry lists the ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics among its codes of practice and guidelines, but this is a regional document rather than a national one. The 2025 Cybersecurity Law appears to contain no AI provisions. A Digital Economy Roadmap 2030 and a Digital Government Master Plan may contain AI content.
narrative.review_notes: Not yet verified from the official text: the 2025 Cybersecurity Law, the Digital Economy Roadmap 2030 and the Digital Government Master Plan 2023-2030. Official sources checked in October 2026 include the telecommunications regulator, the cyber emergency team, the central bank and the foreign affairs and education ministries, with no national AI documents identified; still to check: the national legislation portal, parliament and the planning and finance ministry websites.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Myanmar's laws, government, ministries and the central bank were searched in English and Burmese for AI laws, strategies and guidance. No qualifying AI-governance document was found in any category; an unofficial translation of the cybersecurity law shows no AI provisions, and two digital plans are listed as leads. The official text of the cybersecurity law remains to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. mlis.gov.mm reset/503; motc.gov.mm HTTP 521; mopf.gov.mm refused/unresolvable; mofa.gov.mm, mcf.gov.mm and mdeb.gov.mm unreachable. cbm.gov.mm reached (no AI results). Cybersecurity Law No. 1/2025 checked only in an unofficial translation (no AI terms); not recorded. Not a party to Convention 108. Units covered: Law: Searched for AI laws and AI provisions (English and Burmese). The Myanmar Law Information System (mlis.gov.mm) was unreachable (connection reset; HTTP 503). The Cybersecurity Law (Law No. 1/2025, in force 30 July 2025 by Notification 113/2025) was checked via a discovery copy of its English translation: no AI, algorithm or deepfake provisions, so not recorded. No data protection law with automated-decision rules; no AI bill found. Searched, nothing found.; Government: No national AI strategy, AI policy, AI governance framework or public-sector AI guidance found. Digital Economy Roadmap 2030 and Digital Government Master Plan 2023-2030 held as leads (AI content unverified; official sites unreachable).; Ministries: Ministry of Transport and Communications (motc.gov.mm returned HTTP 521), Ministry of Planning and Finance (unreachable), Ministry of Foreign Affairs (connection reset); education, science and technology, health searched by web search: no AI documents found.; Regulators: Central Bank of Myanmar site search for 'artificial intelligence' and 'AI': no results. No separate data protection authority exists; cyber security functions sit with the ministry under the Cybersecurity Law; no AI-specific regulator documents found.. Not reached: mlis.gov.mm (legislation portal) unreachable; motc.gov.mm unreachable (HTTP 521); mopf.gov.mm unreachable (proxy CONNECT refused; WebFetch DNS failure); mofa.gov.mm (connection reset); mcf.gov.mm, mdeb.gov.mm unreachable. leads.title: Myanmar Digital Economy Roadmap 2030
leads.issuing_authority: Digital Economy Development Committee (chaired under the de facto authorities' administration)
leads.note: Reported as launched in December 2024 (strategic pillars and 77 action plans); a roadmap PDF is linked from the Ministry of Planning and Finance site (mopf.gov.mm 'RoadMap for Websites.pdf'), but mopf.gov.mm and motc.gov.mm could not be reached on 2026-10-12 (curl and WebFetch both failed), so its AI content, title and date are unverified. Check whether it contains an AI pillar or AI action items; record as strategy only if it does. 2026-10-18: mopf.gov.mm still could not be reached (host name does not resolve), and the communications regulator's frameworks and policies list does not carry the roadmap; AI content still unverified. Update 2026-11-08: a state news page (https://www.mdn.gov.mm/en/node/188391) reports that the Digital Economy Development Committee released the Roadmap on 24 December 2024 with 1 vision, 1 mission, 6 goals, 9 priority sectors, 9 strategic pillars, 22 strategic goals and 77 action plans; the page does not mention AI. The planning ministry PDF ('RoadMap for Websites.pdf') was not opened (robots exclusion). AI content still not confirmed. 2026-11-07: A state news page (https://www.mdn.gov.mm/en/node/188391) reports the Digital Economy Development Committee released the Roadmap on 24 December 2024 with 1 vision, 1 mission, 6 goals, 9 priority sectors, 9 strategic pillars, 22 strategic goals and 77 action plans; it does not mention AI. The mopf.gov.mm PDF ('RoadMap for Websites.pdf') was returned by search but could not be retrieved. AI content still unverified. The issuing bodies operate under the military-led administration in place since February 2021, whose legitimacy is contested internationally.

leads.title: Digital Government Master Plan (2023-2030)
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Transport and Communications (as listed in an ASEAN overview)
leads.note: Listed as 'in progress' in a 2024 ASEAN overview of member-state AI policies; no official text found online on 2026-10-12. Check for AI provisions once published. 2026-10-18: not found on the Posts and Telecommunications Department's laws, frameworks/policies or guidelines listings; motc.gov.mm still unreachable. Update 2026-11-08: a state news page (https://www.mdn.gov.mm/my/node/174671) reports e-Government Steering Committee meeting 1/2024 at the Ministry of Transport and Communications, chaired by the Union Minister for Transport and Communications, saying the e-Governance Master Plan (2016-2020) was revised into the 'Myanmar e-Governance Master Plan 2030' (also called 'Myanmar e-Government Master Plan 2030'); no AI mention and no document link. An aggregator page (https://dig.watch/resource/myanmar-e-governance-master-plan-2030-draft) lists a 'Myanmar e-Governance Master Plan 2030 (Draft)' by the same ministry, undated, said to refer to analytics and AI for data-driven public-sector decisions and to 'blockchain, AI, and IoT for governance'. Probably the same document as this item; no official text found. Authority status: the ministry operates under the administration in office since February 2021, whose legitimacy is contested internationally. 2026-11-07: An aggregator (dig.watch, discovery only) lists a 'Myanmar e-Governance Master Plan 2030 (Draft)' by the Ministry of Transport and Communications, undated, said to refer to analytics/AI for data-driven public-sector decisions and 'blockchain, AI, and IoT for governance'; probably the same document as this plan. No official copy found. The issuing bodies operate under the military-led administration in place since February 2021, whose legitimacy is contested internationally.

leads.title: Draft National AI Strategy (NAS) and National AI Policy (NAP)
leads.english_title: Draft National AI Strategy (NAS) and National AI Policy (NAP)
leads.note: Known only from a personal blog (11 March 2025) citing a Myanmar International TV item: the Ministry of Science and Technology held its fourth coordination meeting on 18 February 2025, under Union Minister Dr. Myo Thein Kyaw, to draft a National AI Strategy and a National AI Policy (aims: AI in development sectors, ethical guidelines and standards, skills, international collaboration). A US trade.gov market-intelligence page says the government 'continues to draft' a 'National AI Strategy (2025-2030)'; that period may be confused with Cambodia's draft of the same name. No official text or ministry page found; check most.gov.mm, mdn.gov.mm and the Union Gazette for a published or consultation draft. Authority status: the ministry operates under the administration in office since February 2021, whose legitimacy is contested internationally.

leads.title: Myanmar Digital Economy Roadmap - Strategies and Action Plans (2018/2019 edition)
leads.english_title: Myanmar Digital Economy Roadmap - Strategies and Action Plans (2018/2019 edition)
leads.note: Known from an aggregator page (https://dig.watch/resource/myanmar-digital-economy-roadmap): roadmap of the Digital Economy Development Committee (chaired by the Union Minister of Planning and Finance), drafted 2017-2018, with four pillars, nine priority sectors and 14 goals; no AI mention in that summary. Possible predecessor of the Digital Economy Roadmap 2030. The planning ministry's 'RoadMap for Websites.pdf' may be this edition or the 2030 one. Relevant to the historical category only if the official text has an AI element.
